summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, seizure disorder, diabetes, and bipolar disorder was admitted after experiencing a seizure triggered by severe right-sided abdominal pain that began while lifting bags. He also reported nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and fever. Imaging confirmed chronic calcific pancreatitis with no acute features and interval removal of a prior pancreatic stent. His white blood cell count was elevated, and he had a seizure during a CT scan. He was managed with pain control, pancreatic enzymes, and adjustment of his Dilantin dose due to subtherapeutic levels. His diet was advanced from clear liquids to a low-fat diet, and he remained seizure-free. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue medications, avoid heavy lifting, and follow up with GI and neurology.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
